transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm a 32-year-old medical-surgical nurse, and no matter how many lists and reminders I use, I keep forgetting everyday work tasks and follow-ups, and it’s starting to affect my job. This has been a major struggle for about two years since my hospital transitioned to a new EHR system. It recently led to formal feedback about my reliability, and I'm deeply concerned about patient safety and my career.
Have you noticed any difficulties with focusing or paying attention to tasks, or is the primary issue remembering to do them after they've been set as tasks or reminders?

Honestly, it’s a combination of both. When I’m trying to focus on a task like charting, my mind easily drifts or my eyes will skim right over important details and I'll miss things. At the same time, even when I have flags and alarms set up to remind me, I still routinely forget to actually follow up on those tasks later in the shift.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, feeling restless, or having an urge to constantly be on the move, especially during periods when you're supposed to be focused on a task?

No, I don't really feel physically restless or have an urge to constantly move. My struggles are much more about my mental focus, like my mind drifting off and forgetting tasks, rather than any kind of physical hyperactivity.

Do you experience feelings of anxiety, guilt, or significant distress related to your forgetfulness and difficulty with focusing, or is your main concern more about the practical impact on your job and patient safety?

It is deeply both, because the practical impact on my job and patient safety is exactly what causes me so much anxiety. I am constantly terrified that I will miss something critical that actually harms a patient, which has led to endless worry and feeling like I can't trust my own memory anymore.

Can you tell me more about when these feelings of anxiety and guilt started, and if they have been constant since you began experiencing difficulties with focus and memory, or if they have intensified over time?

I don't really experience clinical anxiety or guilt per se, but rather a constant sense of worry, fear, and alarm about my work performance and patient safety. This has definitely intensified over the last two years as my work demands grew and I realized my coping routines weren't enough anymore. It's gotten to the point where I'm constantly on edge during my shifts, terrified I'll miss something critical.

You mentioned earlier that you don't feel physically restless, but can you tell me if you've ever experienced periods of excessive talking, interrupting others, or feeling impatient when waiting for your turn, especially in social or professional settings?

I definitely struggle with overtalking, especially when I'm giving shift reports or trying to explain a situation to my colleagues. I tend to give way too much detail, and even though I notice people glazing over or trying to cut in, I find it really hard to rein myself in and get to the point. I don't really interrupt others or feel impatient, but the overtalking is definitely a challenge.
Have you ever found yourself blurting out answers before questions have been completed, or having difficulty waiting for your turn in conversations, aside from the overtalking you mentioned?

No, I don't really experience blurting out answers or having trouble waiting my turn in conversations. My main struggle with communication is definitely just that tendency to overtalk and ramble on once I actually get started.

Can you describe how your difficulties with focus, memory, and communication, such as overtalking, affect your daily life outside of work, and if you've noticed any similar patterns in your personal relationships or hobbies?

I haven't really thought about how this impacts my personal life or hobbies, to be honest. My focus and stress have been almost entirely consumed by my struggles at work lately, so I'm not quite sure how it plays out in other areas.
Do you experience difficulties with focus, memory, or communication, such as overtalking, in situations outside of your work, like with friends, family, or during leisure activities?

I haven't really noticed these difficulties as much outside of work, mostly because my home life is much less demanding. My focus and energy are so consumed by trying to keep up at the hospital that I haven't paid much attention to how it affects my personal life. It's really my job and my patients that I'm most worried about right now.

Have you ever felt like you act on impulse without fully thinking through the consequences, such as blurting out things you later regret or doing things without considering the impact, outside of the overtalking you've mentioned?

No, I don't really experience impulsivity or acting without thinking. Aside from that tendency to overtalk and go into way too much detail that I mentioned, I don't really do or say things impulsively.

Can you help me understand if your difficulties with focus, memory, and overtalking have been present since childhood, or if they seem to have started or significantly worsened around the time your hospital switched to the new EHR system?

While the new EHR system two years ago definitely stripped away my ability to cope and made this a crisis, these struggles actually go all the way back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, I was constantly forgetting my homework, losing permission slips, and needing my mom to sit right next to me just to finish simple worksheets because my mind would drift off. The recent transition at work just made these lifelong tendencies impossible to manage anymore.

Can you clarify if these lifelong difficulties with focus, memory, and overtalking have been relatively consistent over time, or have there been periods where they significantly improved or worsened, especially before the recent challenges at work?

They’ve always been there, but I managed to keep them under control during school and my early nursing career by relying on incredibly strict, rigid routines. But when the hospital transitioned to the new EHR and complex workflows two years ago, those coping mechanisms completely failed. That's when my struggles escalated dramatically and became impossible to manage on my own.
You mentioned that these difficulties started in childhood, but can you tell me more about how they presented back then and if you received any diagnosis or interventions for them?

In elementary school, I constantly lost permission slips in my desk, forgot my homework, and my mind would drift so much that my mom had to sit right next to me just to get through simple worksheets. I never received a formal diagnosis or any professional help back then, so her constant supervision and hand-holding was really my only coping mechanism.

Were you ever evaluated for or did you receive any accommodations for these difficulties with focus and memory during your school years, such as an Individualized Education Program (IEP) or a 504 plan?
No, I don't recall ever being formally evaluated back then. I certainly never received any official accommodations like an IEP or a 504 plan during my school years.

Can you describe any significant events, stressors, or changes in your life or environment that you think might have triggered or worsened your symptoms around the time they became more pronounced, aside from the transition to the new EHR system at work?

There really weren't any other major personal or life stressors happening for me at that time. The transition to the new EHR and the much more complex care pathways at work were the main disruptions that completely overwhelmed my ability to cope. That change alone was what broke my routines and caused everything to pile up.

Can you confirm if your difficulties with focus, memory, and overtalking have been persistent since childhood, or if there have been any periods where you felt you were able to manage them effectively without significant impairment?

Yes, they have been persistent since childhood, but I was able to manage them for years without major impairment by relying on incredibly strict, rigid routines through school and early in my career. However, that coping system completely broke down about two years ago when the hospital transitioned to the new EHR and more complex multitasking demands. Since then, those old strategies just haven't been enough to keep me from falling behind.

Can you confirm if your difficulties with focus, memory, and overtalking have been persistent since childhood, and did you ever experience a period of significant improvement or remission before the recent challenges at work?

Yes, they have definitely been persistent since childhood, and I never actually had a period of remission or improvement. I only managed to succeed academically and professionally by relying on incredibly strict routines and constantly over-compensating to get by. Those struggles were always there under the surface until the overwhelming changes at work two years ago finally broke through my coping mechanisms.

Have you experienced significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning as a result of your symptoms, and if so, can you describe how they have affected your relationships or daily life outside of work?

The impairment at work has been severe—my manager has formally flagged my reliability, I've been passed over for a charge nurse role, and I’m constantly terrified I'll make a mistake that harms a patient. While I do have some minor forgetfulness at home, the truly distressing and major impact is entirely centered on my professional life right now.

Given that your difficulties with focus, memory, and overtalking have been persistent since childhood, can you confirm if these symptoms have been relatively consistent over time or if they have significantly worsened with age, particularly in response to increasing demands or stressors?

Yes, while I've always had these tendencies, they became significantly worse and harder to manage as my responsibilities grew, culminating in a major crisis about two years ago. My strict routines worked well enough until the hospital transitioned to the new EHR and complex care pathways, which vastly increased my multitasking demands. That increased cognitive load completely overwhelmed my coping mechanisms, causing my symptoms to escalate into major struggles at work.

Can you describe any specific situations or tasks outside of work where you feel your difficulties with focus and memory are most pronounced, such as during hobbies, reading, or conversations with friends and family?

I haven't really noticed these issues as much outside of work, mostly because my home life doesn't require the same intense multitasking. Besides, my energy is so entirely drained by trying to keep up with my nursing shifts that I haven't had much time or mental space for hobbies or socializing lately.

Can you think of any situations, either at work or outside of it, where you've been able to focus and complete tasks without significant difficulty or forgetting, and if so, what made those situations different?

In the past, I was able to function well and succeed by relying on very strict, highly structured routines to keep myself on track. However, since the hospital transitioned to the new EHR and complex care pathways that require constant multitasking and rapid changes, those routines no longer work. Now, I find it incredibly difficult to find any situation at work where I can focus easily without feeling completely overwhelmed.
Can you estimate how often you find yourself making careless mistakes or failing to follow through on instructions at work, and has this frequency changed over the past two years?

It happens routinely now, almost every single shift, which is a massive change from two years ago. Ever since the hospital transitioned to the new EHR and complex care pathways, these slip-ups have become a constant daily struggle that I find myself desperately trying to catch at the end of every shift.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any periods of significant improvement or remission in your symptoms since childhood, or have they been consistently present and problematic throughout your life?

They have been consistently present since childhood, and I've never experienced a period where they actually went away or improved. I only managed to keep them somewhat under control in adulthood by relying on extremely strict routines, but they never truly disappeared. Over the last two years since the hospital changed its systems, they have become a constant, overwhelming struggle that I can no longer manage.

You've mentioned that your difficulties with focus and memory have been present since childhood, but can you clarify if you believe these symptoms have been relatively consistent in their impact on your daily life, or if they have significantly worsened over time, particularly in response to specific stressors or changes like the transition to the new EHR system at work?

While the underlying tendencies have been there since childhood, their impact on my daily life has definitely worsened over time. For years I managed to get by with strict routines, but the transition to the new EHR and complex care pathways two years ago completely shattered those coping mechanisms. That specific change made my symptoms much more severe and noticeable, turning what used to be manageable struggles into a constant crisis.

Did your difficulties with focus, memory, and overtalking significantly worsen around the time of the EHR system change at work, or was there a more gradual progression of these symptoms over your lifetime?

I've had milder versions of these struggles, like losing homework and needing constant supervision, since childhood, but I managed to cope using strict routines as an adult. However, the symptoms became significantly worse and completely unmanageable about two years ago when the hospital transitioned to the new EHR and complex care pathways. That change completely overwhelmed my coping strategies, turning a manageable baseline into a severe crisis.

Can you clarify if the worsening of your symptoms around the time of the EHR system change at work was due to the increased demands of the new system itself, or if there were other factors, such as changes in your personal life or additional stressors, that might have contributed to this escalation?

The worsening was entirely due to the new EHR system and the more complex care pathways, which suddenly demanded constant multitasking and rapid protocol changes. My personal life was completely stable with no other stressors at the time. The escalation was purely because the overwhelming cognitive demands of this new work setup completely overrode my previous coping routines.

Can you confirm whether the significant worsening of your symptoms around the time of the EHR system change at work represents a qualitative change in the nature of your difficulties, or merely a quantitative increase in the severity of long-standing symptoms?

It is definitely a quantitative increase in the severity of my long-standing struggles rather than a brand-new type of problem. I've always struggled with forgetfulness and distraction since childhood—like losing homework and permission slips in school—but I used to compensate with strict routines. The new EHR and multitasking demands simply overwhelmed those coping mechanisms, making these lifelong difficulties much more severe and visible.

You've mentioned that your difficulties with focus, memory, and overtalking have been present since childhood, but can you clarify if there was a specific point or period when you first noticed these symptoms, or if they seemed to develop gradually over time?

Looking back, I first noticed these tendencies as early as elementary school, when I'd constantly lose permission slips, forget homework, and need my mom's help to keep my mind from drifting. They were always there but stayed manageable through my strict routines until about two years ago, when the EHR transition at work made them suddenly escalate into a major struggle.
Can you describe any instances where you've been able to sustain focus on a single task for an extended period without getting distracted, either at work or in your personal life?

I honestly struggle to think of any recent examples where I've been able to easily sustain focus on a single task for a long time. Even when I do manage to finish something, I'm usually constantly fighting off distractions or having to forcefully drag my attention back to it the entire time.

Did you experience any notable improvements in your focus, memory, or overtalking symptoms during periods of lower stress or fewer responsibilities, such as during vacations or less demanding periods in your career?

I haven't really noticed a significant improvement during vacations or lower-stress times. Even when I am completely off work, I still find myself being forgetful and overtalking when I'm catching up with people. It seems like those tendencies are always there in the background, regardless of how much pressure I'm under.
